title: The supplied projection mate on a shifted structure sheaf
statement: Use the derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], their canonical K-flat tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback] and direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For a morphism f, an adjunction p:Lf^*\dashv Rf_* with counit \epsilon and a natural isomorphism t:Lf^*(-\otimes^L-)\simeq Lf^*(-)\otimes^L Lf^*(-), write \pi_{p,t}(M,L) for the adjunction transpose of t_{M,Rf_*L} followed by 1_{Lf^*M}\otimes\epsilon_L. Let f:X\to Y be any morphism of schemes, with arbitrary derived localizations in a common morphism universe w, and p,t as above. Let L\in D(\mathcal O_X), M\in D(\mathcal O_Y), k\in\mathbf Z and an isomorphism M\simeq\mathcal O_Y[k]. Then \pi_{p,t}(M,L) is invertible. No quasi-coherence, compactness or separatedness is assumed.

proof.text: The canonical monoidal model of derived pullback identifies its value on the structure sheaf with the structure sheaf. The complex construction gives shift compatibility; tensoring with a shifted structure sheaf is translation.

Under these unit and shift identifications t(O[k],-) is an isomorphism of shifted pullback functors. The shifted adjunction conjugates it to an isomorphism of the corresponding shifted direct images. Expand the Hom-equivalence counit formula to identify this conjugate with the displayed mate. The conjugate of its inverse is its inverse, using the triangle identities. This uses the supplied comparison, not just the canonical tensorator. This is the formal conjugate-equivalence calculation of Mathlib CategoryTheory.conjugateEquiv_iso, after transporting the shift equivalences; it is not the generally false assertion that every mate of an isomorphism is invertible.
Naturality of t, the counit and the Hom equivalence transports the isomorphism from O[k] to M along the given isomorphism. Degree zero and empty schemes use the same formula.
